newsitem.title: USA: Florida college fund to divest tobacco stocks.
newsitem.headline: Florida college fund to divest tobacco stocks.

text.p: Florida's $2 billion college tuition prepayment trust fund will divest tobacco holdings from its investment portfolio, the fund's executive director said Tuesday.

The fund holds $12.8 million of tobacco stock and corporate notes, accounting for less than one percent of its total value. Of that, $11.5 million is in Philip Morris Cos Inc and $1.3 million is in American Brands Inc, the fund's executive director, Tom Wallace, said.
The fund's investment managers were instructed to "use sound investment management strategy and discretion in the orderly divestiture of the holdings."
Money generated from the sales is to be reinvested into companies whose stock performances matches that of the tobacco companies.
The divestiture announcement follows last month's decision by Florida's pension fund managers to divest an estimated $825 million of tobacco stocks from the $60 billion fund covering state workers.
Tuesday's announcement was made by the Florida Prepaid Postsecondary Education Expense Board, which administers the state's prepaid college program.
The program allows parents or others to lock in college tuition costs by making payments at current prices for children in 11th grade or younger.
The money is held in a private trust fund designed to earn enough to cover rising tuition costs when the child enters a state college. The program currently administers 425,000 prepayment contracts.

The tuition fund's board said the divestiture decision was based on the advice of the State Board of Administration. That board, comprised of the governor, comptroller and insurance commissioner, urged the sale of all tobacco stocks held in public trust because of "recent legal actions taken against the tobacco industry by states and private citizens."

Florida is one of 34 states that have sued the tobacco industry to recoup the public cost of treating tobacco-related illnesses. Florida is also the site of several ongoing or pending lawsuits filed by private citizens seeking to recover damages for illness linked to cigarette smoke.
